verdict.rationale: Better Auth's documented design stores all user and auth data in the developer's own database (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and more). Community users confirm they own all the data and that the adapter design makes switching to another provider or library relatively easy, so leaving is possible without vendor lock-in. However, there is no first-party export feature or documented open-format export path; portability comes from the self-hosted database architecture rather than an export capability. missing for 10: a documented export tool or format, an outbound migration/exit guide, and hands-on corroboration of a full exit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Better Auth requires a database to store user data. You can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!
You get all of your auth data in your own db in 1 cli command. You are not tied to any db provider.
It just works and I own all the data.
the nature of their database adapters makes it relatively easy to switch to another provider/library
